transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-09 14:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samira P (Redwood AE), Ethan G (Redwood SE), Lena V (CSM), Priyanka D (Velora Lead ML Eng), Carlos M (Velora Infra), Tara B (Velora Product), Ravi I (Velora SRE)

Summary:
Quick sync on the POC telemetry from last week's microburst run; agreed to run a targeted sequence-length sweep and a streaming hedging pass. Discussed tradeoffs between aggressive KV caching vs tighter seqlen buckets. Next steps and owners captured.

Topics:
- TTFT / first-token variability observed in microbursts
- Streaming handshake and buffer sizing
- Kernel selection for mixed short/long sequences
- VPC/network constraints and SOC two notes for audit logs

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): okay hi everyone thanks for joining on time uh quick roll call and then we'll jump into the numbers, Samira from Redwood here, Ethan, Lena with me.
[02:05] Priyanka (Velora): hey thanks, Priyanka here, Tara and Carlos on from infra, Ravi joining in a few minutes. sorry, noisy background.
[04:10] Ethan (Redwood SE): all good. I want to start with the microburst plot you shared, pri, the 95th spikes around 420 ms for first token with current batching, correct? I pulled the logs and saw similar. there's some jitter when sequences exceed 384 tokens.
[06:12] Priyanka: yeah that's exactly it. our average is fine but we have this tail that kills interactive flows. customers hit worst-case when they paste long returns into the widget.
[08:18] Carlos: to add, our traffic is mixed — 60% < 128 tokens, 30% 128-512, 10% >512. we tried increasing batch size but that bumped latency. we also have an internal rule that anything above 512 should go to background workers.
[10:21] Samira: ok good context. thinking out loud: Redwood had success using seqlen bucketing plus a small streaming fast-path for short sequences, and a separate hedged path for >512 where we accept slightly higher token cost. Ethan, can you sketch the kernel choices?
[12:30] Ethan: sure. current pilot uses the default fused-attention kernel on GPU A, that's great up to ~384 tokens. beyond that, throughput drops and the kernel falls back to a general matmul path on our runtime which increases per-token compute and latency. two options: 1) enable the slab-optimized kernel (we call it slab-k) that keeps KV layout contiguous and helps 512+ sequences, or 2) shard KV across two GPUs for long sequences but that's heavy. For TTFT, the slab-k with prefix cache warmup works best for mid-range sequences.
[14:35] Tara: when you say slab-k, is that supported with our quantized model (4-bit)? we moved to q4 last month, not sure about kernel compatibility.
[16:05] Ethan: good point. slab-k requires a small kernel shim for q4; it's supported but we need a recompile path and a small perf hit for the quantized matmul—we'll estimate that in the sweep. also note some CV words in the logs said KV cash instead of KV cache because the ASR in the demo messed up, ha.
[18:12] Priyanka: (laughs) yeah sometimes the transcript is wild. back to the experiment: we want to avoid double-billing tokens for short chat flows — which config minimizes per-token cost while keeping TTFT below 200 ms for most short queries?
[20:25] Ethan: empirically, for your distribution: keep a short-seq streaming fast-path (<=128) with continuous batching (low-latency window 40ms), use prefix caching aggressively and slab-k for the 128-512 mid-range. For >512 send to a dedicated pool with slightly relaxed SLOs. That keeps TTFT median ~80-120 ms and pushes the tail down.
[22:40] Carlos: question about streaming handshake — we saw some stalls at the connection level on our VPC: occasional 100-200 ms delays due to TCP keepalive policy and our intermediate firewall. Is Redwood able to use a lighter-weight handshake or keep-alive tuning?
[24:15] Samira: we can share a recommended firewall/NAT timeout doc. also we have an option to do a regional routing hop to reduce mid-network retries; SE can send a config. For the private pilot we can test VPC peering which should remove long path variance.
[26:30] Ravi (Velora SRE): I'm here — saw the note about VPC peering. we have strict egress rules and an internal proxy that adds latency. i'd like to run a small end-to-end with peering enabled and no proxy to see delta. can Redwood spin up a test endpoint in our designated az?
[28:05] Ethan: yes, we can set up a dedicated test endpoint in-hosted or private mode. for peering we'll need your subnet ranges, firewall rules, and the service account IP allowlist. Carlos, if you share the diagram we'll produce a checklist.
[30:20] Tara: pricing — if we move certain mid-range traffic to slab kernel in-hosted, do we change cost materially? we need an estimate because product is sensitive to cost per chat.
[32:45] Samira: quick answer: slab-k typically increases GPU utilization per long token but reduces time-in-GPU so net cost per output token is comparable or better for mid-range sequences. we'll send modeled numbers for your distribution from the sweep. also we'll outline hybrid pricing: hosted for short streaming; dedicated pool for >512.
[35:10] Priyanka: security/compliance: we need to validate SOC two controls and audit log retention — for the pilot we require 90-day logs and SSO via SAML. is that supported in the private plane?
[36:30] Samira: yes, Private supports SAML SSO, KMS integration and audit logs. for hosted we have a compliance package; we'll share SOC two and ISO artifacts. small warning: hosted audit retention is 30 days by default, can be extended as an add-on.
[38:05] Carlos: ok please share concrete docs. also on encryption — we want HSM-backed keys, is that possible on the dedicated flow?
[39:40] Ethan: yes, dedicated and private can integrate with customer KMS/HSM. we'll need key policies and a small integration window but it's supported.
[41:00] Tara: one more behavioral note — our users sometimes trigger long generations by mistake; could we do a client-side guardrail that rejects any user-generated prompt over 2k chars and instead routes to background?
[42:20] Samira: yep that's a good product approach, we recommended prompt-length guards in previous pilots. we'll add that to the playbook we send.
[43:35] Priyanka: about the sweep, what parameters will you run? sequence bins? batch size? quant profiles?
[44:50] Ethan: plan: 1) seqlen bins [<=64, 65-128, 129-256, 257-512, >512], 2) batch sizes 1, 4, 8 for short; 2, 4 for mid range, 3) kernel variants slab-k, default fused, and fallback matmul, 4) quant profiles q4 and q8 where available. we'll produce median/95/99 TTFTs plus per-token cost estimate.
[46:10] Samira: ok wrap-up — action owners as captured. we'll schedule follow-up for next Thursday the 17th to review results; Ethan will upload the sweep CSV and a short README to the shared drive; Samira will send pricing and pilot contract; Priyanka/Carlos will share prompts and network diagram. any final quick comments?
[47:30] Priyanka: no, thanks everyone, appreciate the concrete plan.
[47:45] Samira: thanks all. meeting adjourned.

References / Links mentioned: shared drive (link: https://redwood.example/velora/pilot-results), SOC2 artifact (link: https://redwood.example/compliance/soc2.pdf), pilot contract template (link: https://redwood.example/contracts/pilot-template.pdf)

Note: transcript contains a few ASR artifacts (e.g., "KV cash") and speaker overlap near the end when multiple folks acknowledged next steps.
